rows: What drives high vs. low F:B ratio (fungal:bacterial)?
High F:B in forest/no-till/well-structured soils (fungi dominate); low F:B in cultivated/disturbed/wet soils (bacteria dominate)
Why does tillage reduce aggregate stability?
Destroys fungal hyphae and glomalin; disrupts earthworm channels; exposes SOM to decomposition; reduces binding agents
What is the AM fungal arbuscule?
Branched tree-like intracellular structure; the exchange interface for P (fungus) and C (plant)
Why can't AM fungi grow without a plant host?
Obligate symbionts; cannot synthesize their own lipids; depend on plant C supply
What is the rhizosphere priming effect?
Root exudates stimulate microbial decomposition of old SOM; up to 300% increase in mineralization near roots
Bacteria immobilize N; protozoa graze bacteria; excrete excess N as NH4+; makes N plant-available
Which mycorrhizal type processes complex organic N?
EM fungi (boreal/temperate trees); produce proteases; access N from forest organic matter
